newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rail strike drags on in southeastern France.
newsitem.headline: Rail strike drags on in southeastern France.

text.p: A rail strike over proposed job cuts dragged on for a sixth straight day in southeastern France on Saturday, disrupting regional train service and some longer lines, railway officials said.

Union representatives and managers from the SNCF national rail authority held negotiations into the early morning hours but failed to reach agreement and new talks were scheduled for Saturday afternoon.
High-speed TGV trains and lines serving Riviera cities along the Mediterranean coast were unaffected by the work stoppages.
But in the remainder of the region, up to 80 percent of regional trains were cancelled.
Train service was also cut back on key lines running between Nice and such major urban centres as Paris, Bordeaux, Strasbourg and Nantes.

The two most powerful SNCF unions have asked members to join a nationwide strike called for October 17 by civil service unions to press for a pay raises and protest against the centre-right government's plans to cut 6,000 jobs next year.
Railworkers led a crippling 24-day public sector strike late last year when Prime Minister Alain Juppe proposed ending early pension rights -- plans which have since been scrapped.

The concern this time is over programmed job cuts and a modernisation plan under which the government will take 125 billion francs ($25 billion) of debt off the loss-making SNCF by spinning it off into another state company which would also become owner of the track and other infrastructure.
Unions fear the plan could open the way to additional staff cuts or a possible privatisation of the SNCF.
